question: Can a beginner use a GA voicing answer to select and play a useful C-major shape without treating the difficulty score as a personal guarantee?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
learner_task: read fret array compare candidates play and listen
hypothesis: A fixed C-major shape comparison and GA's ranked service contract can teach a novice to make a tentative choice, then check the sounding notes and physical comfort on a guitar.
evidence: GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924: Apps/ga-server/GaApi/Services/VoicingFilterService.cs returns fret arrays and difficulty metadata ordered by ascending difficulty score.

The same commit: Tests/Apps/GaApi.Tests/Services/VoicingFilterServiceTests.cs checks nonempty C results, ascending score, and filter behavior; 18 focused GA voicing/comfort tests passed locally with --no-build on 2026-10-05, so the test binary was not rebuilt.
state/streeling/fixtures/guitar-studies/gtr-003/voicing-comparison.json contains three hand-checked C-major teaching shapes; they are not asserted to be GA generator output.
No observed novice play-through, physical comfort judgment, or live UI check has been recorded.
